# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 14
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 14

---

*[After the martyrdom. Thomas appears to Siphor and the community. The king's son Misdaeus is healed by dust from Thomas's tomb. Final conversions and closing.]*

1. And after Thomas was buried, the believers gathered together and were filled with grief and fasting.

2. And at night Thomas appeared to Mygdonia and said to her: "Daughter, be not afraid, for I have not left you. My Lord Jesus Christ in whom I believe is with you and with all those who believe in him."

3. And Mygdonia took courage and told the others what she had seen.

4. And after some days the king's son Misdaeus had a son who was possessed by a demon, and he afflicted him greatly.

5. And Misdaeus thought to himself: "I will go to the tomb of that man of God and take some of the bones and place them upon my son, and perhaps my son will be healed."

6. And he went to the tomb but he did not find the bones there, for one of the brothers had taken them and carried them to the West.

7. But Misdaeus took dust from the place where the bones had lain, and he put it upon his son.

8. And the son was healed at once.

9. And Misdaeus believed in our Lord Jesus Christ and was baptized.

10. And he said: "I believe in you, O Lord Jesus Christ, and I am asking you now to forgive me for what I have done against your servant Thomas."

11. And many in India were converted and came to believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, both men and women, young and old.

12. And the churches which Thomas had established were maintained and grew and multiplied.

13. And the whole story of what was done in India, all the miracles and all the signs, have been written down so that those who come after may know and believe.

14. Now the glory be to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and for ever and ever. Amen.

---
*EMET note: Misdaeus's conversion (vv.9–10) is the final irony of the ATH: the man who condemned Thomas to death is converted by the dust of Thomas's tomb. Thomas's martyrdom accomplishes what his preaching could not compel. The relics translated to the West (v.6) is an early witness to the tradition of Thomas's bones going to Edessa (modern-day Urfa, Turkey).*
